hints: Take logarithms so that the powers become coefficients of $x$.
Collect the terms containing $x$ on one side, then evaluate the resulting exact quotient and round only at the end to 2 decimal places.
walkthrough:
Take natural logarithms of both sides of the given exponential equation $2(3^{2x-1}) = 4^{x+1}$:
$$\ln\left[2(3^{2x-1})\right] = \ln\left(4^{x+1}\right)$$

Apply the product rule $\ln(ab) = \ln a + \ln b$ to the left side and the power rule $\ln(u^k) = k\ln u$ to both sides:
$$\ln 2 + \ln\left(3^{2x-1}\right) = (x + 1)\ln 4$$
$$\ln 2 + (2x - 1)\ln 3 = (x + 1)\ln 4$$

Expand the products on both sides:
$$\ln 2 + 2x\ln 3 - \ln 3 = x\ln 4 + \ln 4$$

Collect the terms involving $x$ on the left-hand side and the constant terms on the right-hand side:
$$2x\ln 3 - x\ln 4 = \ln 4 + \ln 3 - \ln 2$$
$$x(2\ln 3 - \ln 4) = \ln 4 + \ln 3 - \ln 2$$

Simplify the coefficient of $x$ using the power and quotient rules of logarithms:
$$2\ln 3 - \ln 4 = \ln(3^2) - \ln 4 = \ln 9 - \ln 4 = \ln\!\left(\dfrac{9}{4}\right) = \ln(2.25)$$

Simplify the right-hand constant expression using the product and quotient rules of logarithms:
$$\ln 4 + \ln 3 - \ln 2 = \ln(4 \times 3) - \ln 2 = \ln 12 - \ln 2 = \ln\!\left(\dfrac{12}{2}\right) = \ln 6$$

Evaluate the numerical logarithms to high precision:
$$\ln 6 \approx 1.79175947$$
$$\ln(2.25) \approx 0.81093022$$
$$x = \dfrac{1.79175947}{0.81093022} \approx 2.209511 \dots$$

Round the answer to 2 decimal places:
$$x = 2.21$$
